findings.reason: unless the node names the shared list and says whether it shrinks or splits it, the code calibration keeps querying removed properties and path discovery loses dimensions it still writes.
findings.text: §25's `code-score-through-jev` retires seven CodeFile `score_*` dimensions and `file_category` and adds `score_signal_processing`, `score_machine_description`, `score_imas_mapping` and `relevance_grade`, but the plan names no owner of the code score model: `CODE_SCORE_DIMENSIONS` (scoring.py:21) and `CodeScoreFields` (scoring.py:114) are that owner, `SCORE_DIMENSION_NAMES` defined as `CODE_SCORE_DIMENSIONS` at imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py:41, and `sample_code_dimension_calibration` (scorer.py:183) queries `CodeFile.{dimension}` once per entry (scorer.py:241) — so the seven retirements must be reconciled with that list, which path discovery also builds on (`PATH_SCORE_DIMENSIONS = CODE_SCORE_DIMENSIONS + PATH_EXTRA_DIMENSIONS`, scoring.py:40).

findings.reason: an implementer following the plan literally would add a duplicate helper and re-plan landed nodes; the plan must record the census so §14's and §25's node lists match the tree.
findings.text: §14's code-claims node describes adding "one helper beside the renderer ... that returns the clause and its parameters together"; `build_path_prefix_filter` already exists (query_builder.py:283) with exactly that contract (empty clause and no parameters on an empty list), is already used by the path claims (imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:501,562,624,747,832) and two code claims (imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:134,310), and is pinned by tests/graph/test_path_prefix_filter.py; the same census holds for §25's `decisions-call` (call_decisions/acall_decisions already at imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3435/3499, `_service_headers` at llm.py:1995, the `discovery-relevance` seat at imas_codex/settings.py:148, `CODE_RELEVANCE_EXPR` at imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py:63, the eight `relevance_*` fields at imas_codex/graph/models.py:16962, and a second decisions consumer at imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:297).

findings.reason: two stored/computed owners of one quantity drift, and a shared dimension carrying two producers needs the plan to say whether path and code may diverge, or to give the code facet its own field.
findings.text: §25 makes `score_composite` "the largest of the four scope nouls, the value the ingest gate reads", a second owner of a quantity the live tree already computes as `CODE_RELEVANCE_EXPR` (scorer.py:63), which is what the triage and ingest claims and their ordering actually compare (imas_codex/discovery/code/parallel.py:452; graph_ops.py:416,442,703); `score_composite` is separately read by the ingestion queue (imas_codex/ingestion/queue.py:179) and search (imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:1559). The same shape appears for `score_data_access` (scoring.py:25), a shared `CODE_SCORE_DIMENSIONS` entry that path discovery already writes with the LLM-rubric meaning (imas_codex/discovery/paths/scorer.py:462,605; imas_codex/discovery/paths/models.py:321).

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `call_decisions`/`acall_decisions` (imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3435) hide endpoint, auth, retry, per-type validation and cost behind one `(answers, cost)` pair, and the validator is extended in place rather than wrapped.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §25 gives CodeFile's shared score properties (`score_composite`, `score_data_access`) a second producer beside the mechanism that already owns each quantity.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §25's Interface account names what it retires (eleven CodeFile fields, the `code/triage.md` LLM rubric, code's use of the `discovery-triage` seat and `get_triage_threshold()`, and ingest's reading of `--min-score`), so no section adds surface without an account.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §14 and §25 describe as to-be-added machinery that already exists in the tree (the decisions call layer, the path-prefix clause helper, the relevance fields), and §25 omits the shared owner of the code score model it is about to rewrite.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only new layer the plan names, `_service_headers(service)`, is extracted so the chat and decisions paths share one definition, and the plan states why decisions cannot route through `call_llm_structured` (different request and response shape).
